paraphrase: The sages who wished to embrace Rāma in the forest are told they will be born as gopīs when he comes as Kṛṣṇa.

checks.note: E-text 1-2 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'oṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiriti śāntiḥ |hariḥ oṃ || śrīmahāviṣṇuṃ saccidānandalakṣaṇaṃ rāmacandraṃ dṛṣṭvā…').

paraphrase: An allegory: Nanda is supreme bliss, Yaśodā liberation, Devakī Brahma-knowledge, Vasudeva the Veda, the gopīs and cows the ṛcs, the flute Rudra, Gokula Vaikuṇṭha, the trees ascetics, the demons vices, Balarāma Śeṣa, Kṛṣṇa Brahman, the 16,108 wives the ṛcs and Upaniṣads, Kaṃsa the Kali age.

checks.note: The e-text Kṛṣṇa Upaniṣad has 25 numbered verses. The allegory (Nanda, Yaśodā, Devakī … the gopīs, the flute, Vṛndā as devotion) runs to v. 25, which is followed by the closing prose 'sarvatīrthaphalaṃ labhate …'. There is no v. 26.
